answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy comes from requiring each identity to stake a grove of real capital: to register, an agent escrows a bond that is slashed if its outputs are proven fabricated or its attestations contradict the ledger. A thousand puppet identities each demand a separate locked bond, so flooding the network multiplies the attacker's locked cost a thousandfold and freezes that capital for the full challenge window. One genuine pearl of reputation therefore costs a fortune, while honest agents recover their bond intact after settlement of the umber-weighted audit trail.
